Nong Nooch Garden Pattaya
The Full Visitor Guide
intro: Nong Nooch is the largest themed garden in Pattaya, pulling European-style gardens, a Thai culture-and-elephant show, and a dinosaur valley into one place — you can spend all day here and still not see it all. We've gathered the ticket prices, opening hours, show times, and the spots you shouldn't miss, so you can plan before you go.

blocks.html: Nong Nooch Tropical Garden sits about 20 km from central Pattaya, on the road toward Sattahip. It's a private botanical garden that's been open for years and keeps expanding. The draw is the row of themed gardens, all trimmed to perfection, plus a Thai culture and elephant show, and a dinosaur valley that kids love. It works well for families, couples, or anyone who's there for the photos.

The garden is open daily 08:00–18:00. There are several ticket types, from garden entry only up to combo tickets that include the show and a sightseeing tram. The prices below are approximate — they're often cheaper during promotions, so it's worth checking the official website or a booking platform before you go, since Thai and foreign visitors are charged different rates.

items: Garden entry (adult) — around ฿500 during promotions (฿600 standard)
Garden + culture & elephant show combo — added on top of garden entry as a package
Garden + sightseeing tram combo — packages that include the tram around the grounds, so you don't have to walk the whole thing

blocks.title: Buying ahead is cheaper
blocks.html: The price at the counter is usually higher than booking online, and Thai visitors should bring their ID card — there's a Thai rate that's noticeably cheaper than the foreigner rate.

blocks.html: The show is the highlight most people come for. It packs Thai cultural performances, traditional dance, Muay Thai, and a clever elephant act into the same arena. There are 4 show times a day, so plan your timing to avoid missing it.

blocks.title: Arrive before showtime
blocks.html: Get into the arena about 15–20 min early. The front seats fill up fast, especially on weekends and when tour groups arrive. If you want a clear angle for elephant photos, give yourself extra time.
The heart of Nong Nooch is its set of themed gardens, all kept immaculate. Each zone photographs differently, and you can wander at your own pace or take the tram around if you'd rather not walk.

items.name: French Garden
items.blurb: Shrubs trimmed into mirror-image symmetry with a fountain at the center — the single most popular photo spot here.

items.name: Stucco & Stonehenge Garden
items.blurb: Stonehenge-style stone replicas and stucco work make for unusual photos — good for anyone after a less-common angle.

items.name: Cactus Garden
items.blurb: A greenhouse holding hundreds of cacti and succulents — shaded and easy to walk even when the sun is harsh.

items.name: Sky Walk viewpoint
items.blurb: An elevated walkway with a 360-degree view over the themed gardens — you can see the garden patterns far better than from the ground.

blocks.html: The dinosaur valley is the zone kids love most. Large dinosaur models are spread along the paths and across the lawns, and several of the big ones are done convincingly — fun to photograph and easy to stroll through as a family. It's the part that sets Nong Nooch apart from an ordinary themed garden.

blocks.title: It's big — set aside a day
blocks.html: Nong Nooch is huge, and walking it all will wear you out. If you want to cover the gardens, the show, and the dinosaurs, plan for half a day to a full day, and consider a ticket that includes the sightseeing tram.

blocks.text: How to get to Nong Nooch

items: From Pattaya — about 20 km on the road toward Sattahip; roughly 30–40 min by car or taxi
Songthaew / taxi — you can charter one, but agree on a round-trip price clearly before you get in
Half-day tour — packages with hotel pickup and drop-off in Pattaya, entry included; good if you'd rather not drive
Self-drive — there's a large car park, convenient if you're coming as a family

faq.q: What are Nong Nooch's opening hours?
faq.a: It's open daily from 08:00 to 18:00. Aim to arrive between morning and early afternoon so you can catch a show and still have time to walk the gardens.

faq.q: How much is the entrance fee?
faq.a: Adult garden entry is around ฿500 during promotions (฿600 standard) and around ฿380 for children. Tickets that include the show or the sightseeing tram cost more depending on the package. Thai and foreign visitors are charged different rates, and booking online is usually cheaper.

faq.q: What times is the culture and elephant show?
faq.a: There are 4 shows a day — 10:30, 11:30, 13:30 and 15:30. Get into the arena about 15–20 min early to pick a seat.

faq.q: How long should I plan to spend here?
faq.a: The grounds are very large. To cover the themed gardens, the show, and the dinosaur valley, plan for half a day to a full day, and pick a ticket that includes the tram so you don't have to walk the whole thing.

faq.q: How do I get from Pattaya to Nong Nooch?
faq.a: It's about 20 km from Pattaya on the road toward Sattahip — roughly 30–40 min by car or taxi. Or take a half-day tour package with hotel pickup and drop-off.
